html:
Dumnonia was a kingdom of the Britons in southwest Britain, in what is now Devon, Cornwall and part of Somerset, after the end of Roman rule. It is on the map for 600 and 700, though the map's shape for it is rough and sits too far north and west.

Its name came from the Dumnonii, the Iron Age tribe of the area. Its people spoke a Brittonic language close to Welsh and were Christian. Many crossed the sea to Armorica, which became Brittany, and the two coasts kept close ties; see Broërec.

From the 600s Wessex pushed west into Devon. A king named Geraint is known from a letter of about 705 and from fighting with Ine of Wessex. By the 800s only Cornwall was left, and it too came under the English kings, while its Cornish language lived on for centuries. Its neighbours across the Severn were the Welsh.
